quote: I already got the panels up there. They already put the panels up there. They did that in one day. I know that don't cost no $32,000.
stewart_read: This is the clearest orphaned_flow trigger in the call — existing system, existing loan, customer already suspicious of the deal — and the rep does not run the orphaned_flow question set.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could be intentionally deferring detailed diagnosis until legitimacy is established, but nothing later shows the rep coming back to run it properly.
coaching_implication: Should have asked: do you own the system or is it a loan/lease, what company, is it working, and size — per orphaned_flow steps.

quote: See, that's not the way because you already have solar. You shouldn't be paying a monthly bill. I'm not I don't
stewart_read: Rep visibly gets confused mid-sentence trying to reconcile the customer's situation with Ion's normal pitch, and doesn't recover with a clean diagnostic question.
alternative_hypothesis: This could be the rep starting to build toward the orphaned_flow questions, but the sentence trails off and is abandoned, not followed through.
coaching_implication: When confused mid-call, pause and ask the orphaned_flow questions directly instead of talking through the confusion out loud.

quote: Put the solar panel in a on a row house?
stewart_read: Customer flags a non-standard home type (row house) which could affect install feasibility/cross-sell (shared roof, HOA, structural) and the rep never probes it.
coaching_implication: Row house / attached home structure should trigger a follow-up question on shared roof ownership or structural constraints before quoting anything.

quote: I know it would cost more than 10,000.
stewart_read: Rep quotes a rough price floor to a customer already burned by a $32k loan — exactly the kind of pricing content the setter schema says to redirect to the specialist.
coaching_implication: Should have used the escape hatch: 'that's exactly what our specialist works out with you' instead of guessing a number to someone already scam-anxious about cost.

quote: let me tell you one thing before anything else. We have been a business since 2013.
stewart_read: Customer's trust_or_scam objection (competitor bankruptcy, sketchy $32k loan) gets a company-legitimacy reassurance instead of a flip that uses his own pain (the bad deal) as leverage for why Ion is different.
alternative_hypothesis: Reassurance is a valid protocol response to scam anxiety, not strictly a miss — but it doesn't advance the call toward any concrete plan.
coaching_implication: Could pair legitimacy statement with a direct next step: 'once you're free of that contract, let's get you a real design so you know what fair actually looks like.'

quote: give me about a month or so, I guess. I gotta try and get out of this contract.
stewart_read: Call ends with a vague 'about a month' timeline, no scheduled callback date, no button-up sequence run at all.
coaching_implication: Rep should have locked a specific callback date/time rather than accepting an open-ended 'about a month.'
